dag_id_prefix_means: A job's Airflow DAG id is this prefix and its id. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py names the DAGs with it, and foundation-api (GET /data-catalog/v1/scheduled-jobs, root ADR-0165) finds each job's run records in the data catalog under the flow its DAG reports as.
description: Every scheduled data job (root ADR-0118, ADR-0122). What a job runs, as whom and with which environment is its systemd service in infra/systemd. Its time limit is time_limit_minutes here, rendered into the unit (root ADR-0270 §1). This list adds when it runs, its resource pool, the pipeline-graph edges it carries out (its lineage, read from docs/catalog/pipeline-graph.v1.json) and whether Airflow runs it yet. A job that checks data rather than moving it names no edges and sets reads_data_contracts: its inputs are the tables the data contracts cover.

spark.description: The host's scheduled heavy work (root ADR-0138): FLOOR and lineage take all three slots (20g Spark) and run alone; a map-edit fold takes two, so the folds never overlap (their Spark runs share one init container name); the by-PNU bake takes one, so one fold can run beside it; the panel Gold rebuild and each hub Silver refresh lane take all three (20g Spark) and run alone. The host memory guard checks every combination these slots allow.

pools_means: Every Airflow pool a job may name, besides Airflow's own default_pool, with its slot count; a job takes pool_slots of them (1 when absent). scripts/deploy/airflow-runtime.sh creates exactly these. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses a job naming any other pool, a pool_slots above the pool's slots, and a job that could hold slots another job needs for longer than STARVATION_CYCLES runs of that job. scripts/guard/every-container-has-a-memory-cap.sh adds up the memory of every set of jobs the slots let run together (root ADR-0138). compose.orchestration.yml's AIRFLOW__CORE__PARALLELISM is at least the slots here plus one, so a default_pool job always has a slot (orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py). A job's priority_weight decides which waiting job Airflow starts first when slots free (FLOOR and lineage above the folds, the folds above the Silver refresh lanes, the lanes above the Gold rebuild, the Gold rebuild above the bake). retries (1 when absent) is how often Airflow runs it again after a failure. A takes_turns job starts at most once between scheduled starts of every job in its pool that cannot run beside it: scripts/ops/start-scheduled-job.sh keeps the starts and defers it, so a multi-day bake cannot keep FLOOR and lineage waiting run after run.
time_limit_minutes_means: How long one run may run, in minutes: the one number for it (root ADR-0270 §1). The crate foundation-jobs renders it into the TimeoutStartSec= line of the job's systemd unit (`cargo run -p foundation-jobs -- generate`) and its test refuses a unit that says anything else, and jobs that share a unit with different limits. The scheduler's limit for one start is time_limit_minutes + stop_grace_minutes (see stop_grace_minutes_means).
stop_grace_minutes_means: How much longer than time_limit_minutes the scheduler gives one start, in minutes: for the unit to stop and clean up (its TimeoutStopSec) and for the outcome to come back. One start's limit is time_limit_minutes + stop_grace_minutes, and every reader adds the two: the DAG's execution_timeout and SSH timeout and the starvation bound (orchestration/dags/job_specs.py scheduler_timeout_minutes), the deploy's wait for a started-once job (scripts/deploy/foundation-deploy.sh), and when the operations map calls a job late (foundation-api data_catalog/operations.rs). The crate foundation-jobs refuses a grace not longer than the unit's TimeoutStopSec (root ADR-0270 §1). It replaced timeout_minutes, which stated the sum by hand.
wait_limit_minutes_means: How long one scheduled start may wait for the host before its run begins, in minutes (root ADR-0270 §2b, deploy D4): for a release build to finish or for its pool to have room. A start that is still blocked then runs nothing and says so. 0: it never waits. The rule here: a daily default_pool job waits up to 60 minutes (a release build took 2,590 s, measured 2026-10-03 in tools/release-build.contract.json); a job due every hour or half hour waits 0, since its next period is its retry; a spark-pool job waits 0, because a waiting start holds its pool slots and the folds' starvation bound (job_specs) has no room for it — one due during a build is deferred and started by the deploy, until the build leaves the host (root ADR-0276). The scheduler's limit for one start is this plus time_limit_minutes plus stop_grace_minutes (orchestration/dags/job_specs.py scheduler_timeout_minutes); a start the deploy makes directly does not wait and takes the run's limit alone (run_limit_minutes).
state_paths_means: Where a job writes and keeps state across runs, as absolute paths (root ADR-0266). The crate foundation-jobs renders them into the ReadWritePaths= line of the job's ProtectSystem=strict systemd unit and its test refuses a unit that says anything else, and jobs that share a unit with other paths (root ADR-0270 §1). orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses a job script whose state root comes from an EnvironmentFile or defaults outside these paths.
state_directories_means: Every directory the host makes for the jobs, with its mode and owner (account and group of that name; foundation-platform when not stated) (root ADR-0270 §1). The crate foundation-jobs renders them into infra/tmpfiles/foundation-job-state.conf (not infra/host/tmpfiles.d, the retention rules the release cleans with), and the release applies it (systemd-tmpfiles --create) as soon as current switches, before migrate mounts anything, and again in timers: a path a unit or container uses exists with its owner before its first use (the 2026-10-15 class, #625). Each job state path is one of these or is named in state_paths_not_created_here; each of these is a job state path or lies under one. The lakehouse workspaces are 0777: the Spark container (uid 185) writes them. silver-refresh is 2770 so its lanes share the group. No job writes /var/lib/foundation-platform/lakehouse-ivy: every Spark run mounts its release's frozen jars read-only as its Ivy cache (root ADR-0134), so that path is no state path and the release no longer makes it (2026-10-18; the folder is left on the host).
commits_means: When a run commits what it writes (root ADR-0301, ADR-0308). at_end: one commit when the run finishes, so a run stopped midway loses all its work (the onbid collector, 2026-10-26: a timed-out run committed nothing); such a job is never interruptible. as_it_goes: it commits file by file, table by table or pack by pack, or writes nothing a stop could lose, so a stopped run loses at most the unit in progress and its next run continues. Every job states it, so a new collector cannot reach production without saying which; orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py refuses a job that does not, and an at_end job that is interruptible.
scope_means: What one run of the job processes when it has work (root ADR-0314): `changed-keys` only the keys whose content changed since the run before; `new-objects` only the source objects no earlier run recorded; `skip-if-unchanged` one indivisible input (a file, a release, a round, a table snapshot), and nothing when it is unchanged; `full` everything on every run, an exception that states full_reason (why), full_cost (what it measurably costs, dated) and full_tracked_by (the change that makes it partial, or why full is the right unit). scripts/guard/every-job-declares-its-scope.sh refuses a job without a scope, a full job without those three, and a full job tools/ci/full-scope-jobs.baseline.json does not list; that list only shrinks.
interruptible_means: Whether a deploy may stop this job mid-run instead of waiting for it to finish (root ADR-0301). true: the job is append-only/resumable and a partial run is safe (a bake, rebuild, silver load, map-edit fold, boundary release, lakehouse maintenance, lineage, or a per-file-commit source sweep), so a deploy whose release holds it stops it at step 0, records it as owed a run and starts it when it gives the schedule back (root ADR-0308). false: stopping loses a run or leaves a half-written canonical result, so the deploy waits for it; every job whose `commits` is at_end is one (the collectors that commit at the end; they are short), and a few others. Every job states it; orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py refuses a job that does not.

state_directories.written_by: the scheduled jobs' own Prometheus textfiles, each job one <name>.prom it replaces whole (root ADR-0330 §4); node-exporter reads the directory beside the deploy's (root ADR-0321 §5)
foundation-api, the operator switches (root ADR-0282 §3); the gate and the runner only read them

enabled_means: Airflow starts the job's service on the schedule here; its systemd timer is gone from infra/systemd and the release retires it from the host (ADR-0122 §4). A job runs in exactly one of the two places.
enabled_since_means: When the job was switched on, UTC (root ADR-0239): every enabled job states it and a disabled job does not. A scheduled start before it is not a start the job missed, so the operations map never calls a job late for a slot from before it was on. The pull request that switches a job on sets it to the time it is merged; job_specs.py refuses an enabled job without it.
check_service_means: A systemd service that only decides whether the job has work, and a run of it takes no pool slot (root ADR-0277). When a job names one, its DAG runs it first in default_pool as task `check`, through the same host command (`<job> check`, scripts/ops/start-scheduled-job.sh); its last line `foundation-job-check unchanged` skips the run, so a run with nothing to do never waits for its pool. Any other answer, or none, starts the run, which decides again for itself: the check only saves the wait. foundation-release.sh timers grants the scheduler the service as it grants the job's, and every job service's release admission applies to it.
started_by_means: What starts a job (root ADR-0171). `schedule`: Airflow starts it at its schedule. `inputs`: Airflow starts it as soon as a run of another job reports that it changed one of the job's inputs (the pipeline-graph nodes its edges start from), and at its schedule as well, the fallback for what no event announces: a hand load, a run outside Airflow, a run while its DAG was paused, a failed or deferred run. Each input and output is an Airflow asset named by its data catalog dataset; which job feeds which is read from the edges here, never written down a second time. A run says whether it changed its outputs with a last line `foundation-job-outcome changed|unchanged`; only `unchanged` withholds its output events, so a job that does not say counts as changed. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses an `inputs` job no listed job feeds, an enabled one whose feeders are all off, one that writes its own input, and jobs that start each other in a circle.

Parcel lineage stewardship cycle: fold steward decisions, rebuild and load the review queue (root ADR-0115) only when the queue's inputs changed since the last load (scripts/ops/lineage-queue-check.py; otherwise no Spark and no load: gold.lineage_review_queue's 857 rows were last written 2026-10-20). First it loads any pending 필지고유번호변동연혁 handoff into silver.parcel_number_change_history (root ADR-0144 §4), then loads and pairs any pending legal-dong code handoff (root ADR-0143), reading the official links of the pairing window once that table holds rows: the snapshot into reference.legal_dong_code_snapshot, the changes into reference.legal_dong_code_change (the one record of region code changes, root ADR-0145), and the crosswalk projection the hub exports read, a view of that table; a failure there fails the run before lineage starts. Then it derives silver.parcel_lineage (root ADR-0113 §1): for each consecutive pair of the parcel editions the source contract holds, once per sido group (parcel_lineage_scheduled.py), skipping groups already held and starting none after FOUNDATION_LINEAGE_DERIVE_DEADLINE_MINUTES (60), so a backlog spreads over the next runs.

Legal-dong code changes from code.go.kr (root ADR-0143, ADR-0144), the collection half: first ask the site's own change-period filter which codes were created or abolished inside the window the last full run anchored (about 70 KB, root ADR-0322 §2); when it lists the same rows and no full reconcile is owed (code-go-kr-legal-dong.contract.json full_table.changed_since_probe), record the confirmation and stop. Otherwise land the full table (codes, parents, created and abolished dates) in Bronze (requests at least 15 seconds apart; the change-notice board is not a source), refuse a response whose shape changed or a table that shrank past the contract's bounds, record when the table was last confirmed, and, only when the table's rows changed, write a pending-load handoff. No Spark: lineage_stewardship loads and pairs the handoff under its spark slots before its own steps.

VWorld cadastral parcel editions (연속지적도, MK/30563; root ADR-0148): check the provider's newest edition against the source contract (vworld-parcel-source-objects.json); when it is new, collect its directly downloadable files into Bronze, measure each ZIP's members by ranged read, and propose the contract entry. Exit 3 means an edition awaits the contract, not a fault: the job posts 'new edition waiting for contract entry' itself, and is not retried (a retry would only download and propose the same edition again).

Compact and expire every table of the lakehouse contract artifact under the snapshot retention of root ADR-0237 (30 days, 12 month ends, every year end), the least recently maintained first, in one Spark run (infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/lakehouse_maintenance.py --all-tables, root ADR-0238). It starts no table after the maintenance contract's deadline; a table it does not reach is first at the next run. Compaction takes only the small files writes left since the last compaction (a table under the contract's trigger is skipped, and Iceberg leaves files already near the target alone); expiry and the file counts read metadata only (2026-10-29: 48 tables, compaction ran in three of them and read 15, 278 and 0 files). Its volume is therefore what the writers wrote: on 2026-10-26 it rewrote all of gold.parcel_panel because a copy-on-write MERGE had just rewritten all of it (PR #951). Expiry never removes a snapshot a Silver loader or the Gold rebuild reads back. It changes no rows, so it starts nothing downstream.

Reflect each new Gold snapshot of gold.parcel_panel, then gold.building_panel, then each pack-only lane's Gold panel this job carries the served edge of (config/r2-connections.contract.json by_pnu_lanes, root ADR-0190; a lane whose served edge another job carries bakes in that job, root ADR-0303, ADR-0333), in R2 by-PNU serving (root ADR-0096, ADR-0100, ADR-0141): a row_digest change set (by_pnu_panel_delta.py in the spark-small service, sequential with the export) decides between a create-only patch generation of the changed documents and tombstones, a manifest that only advances the reflected snapshot, and a full new base (forced with a reason, a document schema change, max_patches reached, or the cumulative change ratio exceeded). A patch is published only when its shards wrote exactly its change set; a base only when the shards' exported rows add up to the Gold row count. The lanes run one after the other in one unit: side by side they would not fit the host memory budget (root ADR-0138). Once a lane's manifest carries a section_packs block (root ADR-0147; the parcel lane too, ADR-0160), that lane bakes and publishes section packs instead: the change set goes from the packs' reflected snapshot, a patch writes each section's packs under the generation the lane serves it from, and a full bake is a new generation of every section. Started when a Gold rebuild committed a new snapshot, and at 10:15 as the fallback (root ADR-0171); a turn it defers (takes_turns) is taken at the next start, and each lane is an asset of the asset reconciler (asset_reconcile), which starts the job when a lane's Gold moved past what it serves or its last run failed.

Reflect each new Gold snapshot of gold.parcel_public_auction (the own-producer public-auction kind, root ADR-0287) in R2 by-PNU serving (scripts/ops/by-pnu-serving-bake.sh parcel-public-auction), as section packs (root ADR-0147, ADR-0193 §9): a change set decides a create-only patch, a reflect-only manifest or a full new generation, exactly as the panel bake does per lane. Its own job so it bakes concurrently with the panel/parcel bake instead of waiting behind it in `by_pnu_serving_bake all` (root ADR-0303): a slow national parcel re-bake no longer holds public-auction serving for hours (2026-10-28). Own-producer because its servability is resolved at Gold: servable() keeps only the PNUs the served parcel edition carries, which the Gold build reads from Silver (root ADR-0292); the bake reads no parcel lane state, so a PNU of a parcel edition not served yet may 404 until the parcel lane catches up (accepted, root ADR-0303 §2). Started when gold_public_auction_rebuild commits a new snapshot, and at 10:45 as the fallback (root ADR-0171), apart from the panel bake's 10:15 so the two clock starts do not crowd the host at once; each run's containers are its own one-offs (scripts/guard/batch-containers-are-run-scoped.sh). It does not take turns: one slot for at most two hours, which the folds run beside and FLOOR waits out within the pool's starvation bound. One slot and MemoryMax=5G, so it runs beside the panel bake inside the host memory budget (root ADR-0138).

Reflect each new Gold snapshot of gold.unit_price (root ADR-0190) in R2 by-PNU serving (scripts/ops/by-pnu-serving-bake.sh unit-price), as section packs: a change set decides a create-only patch, a reflect-only manifest or a full new generation, as every lane does. Its own job and asset since root ADR-0333, out of `by_pnu_serving_bake all`, where it waited behind the parcel lane (a 20-hour national re-bake on 2026-10-23..28). Its documents follow the building lane's (documents_follow_lane): it bakes a unit price Gold only once the building lane serves a building Gold built from the same register snapshots, and otherwise ends `waiting` until it does, a state the asset reconciler (asset_reconcile) re-checks every five minutes, not a run order inside one unit. Started when gold_unit_price_rebuild commits a new snapshot, by the reconciler when that event was lost or the building lane caught up, and at 10:55 as the fallback (root ADR-0171), apart from the 10:15 and 10:45 bakes so no two clock starts crowd the host at once; each run's containers are its own one-offs (scripts/guard/batch-containers-are-run-scoped.sh). One slot and MemoryMax=3G (root ADR-0138): its whole generation is 169,117 documents in nine shards, and with the parcel and public-auction bakes beside it the pool holds 22g, no more than the release builder.

The asset reconciler (root ADR-0333 §7): every five minutes, for each job it reconciles, compares the version each input of the job's asset is at now (the Iceberg snapshot of a Gold input, or for a pinned input the snapshot its pinning Gold was built from) with the version the asset's last run read (a Gold's recorded source pins; a by-PNU lane's reads.jsonl, which its bake appends), reading only catalog metadata over REST, no Spark and no data file. An asset whose input moved past what it read, that is not running and not waiting on the lane its documents follow, is printed as owed with a key of the versions it owes; its DAG then starts the job once per key (a deterministic run id, so a repeated tick or a lost event never starts it twice), unless a run of it is already queued or running. The trigger only queues the run: it waits for its pool's slots like any other. Writes asset_lag_seconds and asset_unscheduled_seconds per asset for node-exporter (/var/lib/foundation-jobs/metrics/asset-reconcile.prom; the FoundationAsset* alerts), and keeps since when an owed asset has been idle with room in its pool under its state path. Beside them it counts the host's Docker bridge networks against what Docker's address pools hold (docker-networks.prom; FoundationDockerAddressPoolNearlyFull): every job's per-run Compose project takes one, and on 2026-10-29 23 of 31 were taken, 10 by runs whose cleanup had failed. Changes no data: its outcome is always unchanged. It covers the 공매 Gold to bake edge whose event 3912 started nothing on 2026-10-28 (13 hours late), the unit price edges split out by root ADR-0333, and every lane of by_pnu_serving_bake, each its own asset (2026-10-29: its forest-ledger lane failed at 07:41Z and the 10:15 start was deferred by takes_turns, so nothing ran it again). A lane whose last run failed is owed a new start after a backoff (10 minutes doubling to 4 hours); a job serving several lanes is started once for all its owed lanes. The other `inputs` jobs move to it in stage 2.

reconciles_means: The jobs the asset reconciler starts by state rather than by event (root ADR-0333 §7, Kubernetes controllers and Dagster declarative automation are level-triggered the same way). Each named job is an enabled `inputs` job that makes exactly one asset (one output node of the pipeline graph): a Gold table, whose read versions are the source pins its commits record, or a by-PNU lane's section packs, whose read version is the Gold snapshot the lane's last run left served (by-pnu-serving-bake.sh appends it to the lane's reads.jsonl, and a failed run's failure); or a by-PNU bake whose every output is a lane's serving, each lane its own asset (by_pnu_serving_bake, until its lanes are jobs of their own). A job naming `reconciles` carries no pipeline-graph edges: it reads the inputs and outputs of the jobs it reconciles. orchestration/dags/job_specs.py refuses any other shape; scripts/ops/asset_reconcile.py and the reconciler's DAG read this list and nothing else.
started_once_after_deploy_means: The release deploy (scripts/deploy/foundation-deploy.sh, root ADR-0159) starts the job once under the new release, after the switch and before the DAGs are unpaused; a failed run alerts through the unit's own OnFailure and the DAGs are unpaused regardless (root ADR-0173). It marks the jobs short enough to run inside a deploy; the long jobs are left to their schedule (the daily source sweep since root ADR-0172 lets it fetch everything it lacks, which can take hours).
capabilities_means: What a job's release can do that another command checks before relying on it. by_pnu_serving_bake's building_section_pack_patches and parcel_section_pack_patches say the bake patches a lane's section packs once its manifest names them (root ADR-0147, ADR-0160); publish-building-by-pnu-section-packs refuses the first pack publish unless the installed release's job declares it, the capability the building gateway contract names (config/r2-connections.contract.json, building_by_pnu_gateway.section_packs.scheduled_bake).
disabled_reason_means: A job may be listed before Airflow runs it: enabled false, no systemd timer, and disabled_reason says why it is off and what turns it on. The host refuses to start a job that is not enabled (scripts/ops/start-scheduled-job.sh), so a listed but disabled job runs nowhere until a deploy switches it on.
serving_surfaces_without_a_job_means: Every pipeline-graph serving surface whose surface_kind is r2_baked_documents or tiles is produced by a job in this list (a job edge ends at it), or is named here with the reason it has none yet. orchestration/tests/test_job_specs.py refuses a baked surface with neither, and an entry here that is stale (the surface has a job, or is not a baked surface).
